name: Cross-Device Interaction Continuity
description: An interaction pattern that preserves the same conceptual behavior across multiple device form factors while adapting layout and gesture details to each surface.
strengths: Builds a coherent product feel across devices
Makes transitions between surfaces feel intentional
Improves transfer learning for users moving between platforms
failure_modes: Can force unnatural parity across devices
Can become over-abstract if adaptation rules are weak
implementation_notes: Keep the core interaction model stable, but adapt density, gesture vocabulary, and motion timing for each device class rather than copying layouts verbatim.

name: Peel-Back Source Reveal
description: A layered editor interaction where the polished document surface is peeled back or displaced to reveal an underlying source representation such as markdown or structured content.
strengths: Creates a memorable mental model for view/source relationships
Provides high explanatory value in demos and onboarding
failure_modes: May feel theatrical in high-frequency workflows
Needs strong cues to remain discoverable
implementation_notes: Best used sparingly for mode-switching, inspection, or teaching moments. Pair the reveal with strong spatial continuity and obvious return paths.
